title: Bible Guide
paragraph: Keil calls them prophets of the LORD “worshipped under the image of an ox”, who “practised prophesying as a trade without any call from God”. 1 Kings 22:6–7 [1]

blocks.text: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah. He made horns of iron, promised victory over Syria and struck Micaiah on the cheek.
One of Ahab's four hundred prophets, of whom Micaiah said “the LORD hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets” (1 Kings 22:23)
He spoke with “Thus saith the LORD” and acted it out with a sign, the horns of iron.
He spoke with “Thus saith the LORD” and acted it out with a sign, the horns of iron. 1 Kings 22:11
He claimed the Spirit: “Which way went the Spirit of the LORD from me to speak unto thee?” 1 Kings 22:24

From the textKings and Chronicles side by side: Kings has “With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them” and “smote Micaiah on the cheek”; Chronicles has “With these thou shalt push Syria until they be consumed” and “smote Micaiah upon the cheek”. His question about the Spirit is the same in both. 1 Kings 22:11 1 Kings 22:24 2 Chronicles 18:10 2 Chronicles 18:23
“Thus saith the LORD, With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them.”
“Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and prosper: for the LORD shall deliver it into the king’s hand.”
To whom the word was spoken
“With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until thou have consumed them.”
“Which way went the Spirit of the LORD from me to speak unto thee?”
Who stood with him, and against him
Micaiah answered him: “thou shalt see in that day, when thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.” 1 Kings 22:25
The king went up to Ramoth-gilead, was struck by an arrow and died at even. 1 Kings 22:29–37
From the textScripture does not mention Zedekiah again, and does not say whether he hid in an inner chamber. 1 Kings 22:25–40
Prophets of the LORD under the calf worship
Keil calls them prophets of the LORD “worshipped under the image of an ox”, who “practised prophesying as a trade without any call from God”. 1 Kings 22:6–7 [1]
J. Le Clerc and O. Thenius (as reported, and rejected, by Keil, p. 274)
Keil reports that these took them to be “true prophets of Jehovah and disciples of the prophets”. 1 Kings 22:6 [1]
Prophets of Baal or of the groves
“Some of the earlier commentators” (as reported, and rejected, by Keil, p. 274)

Keil reports that some identified them with the prophets of Baal or the four hundred prophets of the groves of 1 Kings 18:19, and answers that Ahab could not have enquired of the LORD through them. 1 Kings 18:19 1 Kings 22:5–6 [1]
Scripture does not say who sent Zedekiah or whom he served besides the king, and gives no other word of his.
Neither Kings nor Chronicles says what happened to Zedekiah after the scene at the gate.
The text does not call him a “false prophet”; it reports Micaiah's word about a lying spirit in the mouth of all the king's prophets.
